answer: Admission requires each new key to forge a one-time work commitment: the applicant publishes a unique job digest that three already-established, non-adjacent peers listed in a public atlas must independently countersign. If two applicants share an operator key, their digests collide in the atlas and both commitments are slashed. Until those signatures land, the identity remains on an island of reduced emission for six epochs, so a farm cannot mint a full share in parallel from one wallet.
